articles.title: THE RISE OF THE SELF-DRIVING COMPANY
articles.summary: Companies pay a lot to keep work moving between people, in meetings and status reports. At Replit, agents are taking on much of that. Designers now ship product changes themselves instead of handing ideas to engineers, and support uses agents to look into customer problems. Engineers wrote nearly three times as much code in the first half of 2026 while review times, rollbacks, and incidents held flat. At most companies, agents still run in chat windows and personal accounts with whatever logins someone handed them, and nobody can see what they did.

articles.title: PAYMENTS MOATS
articles.summary: As AI makes software easier to reproduce, defensibility increasingly rests in regulatory approvals, banking relationships, and accumulated operational knowledge. Records of agent decisions and human corrections can become an advantage that competitors cannot recreate simply by copying the product.

articles.title: THE SIMPLEST, HIGHEST-ROI PLACE TO PUT AN AI AGENT IS YOUR CONTACT ME FORM
articles.summary: Inbound qualification is a good place to start with agent deployments because the job is bounded. The agent just needs to answer questions, qualify, route, and book. There are clear success metrics: meetings booked and revenue closed. The downsides of implementing AI in inbound qualification are low because the alternative is a form that sits in a queue.

articles.title: BETTER AI DIDN'T CHANGE HOW I WORK - HUMANS DID
articles.summary: One AI startup's head of product tried Claude Cowork in January, and it couldn't do the job. A month later, a newly hired product manager showed the head of product how he had Claude Code agents doing his work. Watching a direct report work that far ahead did more than any product demo. That month, the head of product built a first agent to draft the weekly update for leadership. By April, Cowork was running nine jobs. Keep a list of what AI can't do yet, and retry the top items every couple of months.

articles.title: THE FULL CLAUDE PLATFORM, AVAILABLE ON GOOGLE CLOUD
articles.summary: Startups can now spend their Google Cloud commitment on the full Claude Platform, which Anthropic runs and Google bills. Code execution, skills, and web search are included, and new features arrive the same day they do on Anthropic's own platform. Managed Agents and the MCP connector are in beta.

articles.title: REPLIT MONITORING AGENT: YOUR VERY OWN SOFTWARE ENGINEERING TEAM
articles.summary: Replit's Monitoring Agent is an on-call engineer for your published app. It watches for errors and slow responses, investigates each alert, tests a fix, and emails you a summary. It can also republish the fix on its own if you let it.

articles.title: DISCOVER 1000+ SERVICES ON VERCEL CONNECT FROM THE CLI
articles.summary: Vercel Connect CLI now lets users search over 1000 services directly from the terminal using filters like category or connection method. The update supports JSON formatting for scripts and agents, enhancing integration flexibility. Users need CLI version 64.1.0 or later to access these features.

articles.title: THE FORGOTTEN INDUSTRIALIST
articles.summary: AI founders should use George F. Johnson's “Square Deal” framework: share productivity gains among employees, customers, and the business. That means giving employees meaningful ownership, passing savings on to customers, and reinvesting in growth. Lincoln Electric offers a proof point: the company pairs profit sharing with stock returns more than twice the S&P 500's since its 1995 IPO.

articles.title: TOKENS OVER HIRES
articles.summary: Some startups now buy engineering in tokens instead of headcount. Two founders spend about $28,000 a year on AI, less than one engineer costs. In their first month, they merged 657 pull requests. Their biggest bill is about $1,500 a month for an AI code reviewer, so neither founder has to read every first draft. Their real limit is attention. While one founder was reviewing other work, a small database problem grew until it took the product down. So their next engineer will own one piece of the product, agents included.

articles.title: LET CHAOS REIGN, AND THEN REIN IN CHAOS
articles.summary: Some of the first office PCs were expensed as desks or typewriters to get past IT.

articles.title: THE MOST ADVANCED AI ADOPTERS NOW SPEND LESS ON AI
articles.summary: Companies furthest along with AI are starting to spend less on it as cost controls tighten and models get cheaper.

articles.title: WHEN THE ANECDOTES DON'T MATCH THE METRICS
articles.summary: When customers complain but the dashboard looks fine, trust the customers, and fix what the dashboard measures.

articles.title: LOVING UGLY BABIES
articles.summary: Most companies die in the long stretch before anyone cares, and that stretch is where most of the value gets built.
